That's a lovely thought and will be much appreciated.

Is she planning to breastfeed? If so, get in some almonds (apparently the selenium in them is good for BFing mums), dried fruit, raisins etc that she can keep in a small bowl near the sofa to snack on.

Hand cream is good as you're constantly washing them!

Chocolate of course

Any DVDs she might have been wanting to watch

posts.body: Possibly not in the immediate newborn phase, I think we took the prints about the 7 week-ish point - but a necklace or similar with the baby's handprint on it? I've just had one done for my birthday with both my daughters' prints on and it's fabulous... some of the companies will do the print-taking kit in a gift box so you can wrap that up, then do the prints together and send them off and they'll reduce them down and into a silver pendant (or cufflinks or whatever). You can actually really see the features in the handprint they took on my necklace version when it's been shrunk down.

posts.body:
My ideal present would be:

- get her a lasting beautiful present like a piece of jewellery that she can keep forever. I would not like anything baby theme, but each to their own, jewellery is very personal.

- ensure the house was completely cleaned top to bottom for when she came back home from hospital, complete with her favourite flowers and foods in the fridge (if she likes things like pate or proscuitto, she might not have had any for 9 months?)

- give her a care package/goodie basket in hospital of personal, nice things she could use but that may not be to keep "forever", plenty of good suggestions on this thread like chocolates, a subscription to lovefilm, dvds, toiletries etc etc.

She may like something that is all about her, and showing her that she is still your girlfriend, rather than baby related stuff if you see what I mean.

Edited to say, this may sound demanding, and of course I would be happy regardless of any presents, but this would be my ideal list ( and what I would have tried to do for my husband if he was giving birth.....

posts.body:
We're expecting our first in the next 2 weeks! Eeek.

For me I would love to get my hair done properly, get my nails done, and be generally pampered. I've never really enjoyed going to spas and would feel even more uncomfortable while pregnant (but your OH might like spending a day at the spa) so if you have a mobile hair or nail technician in your area that could be a really nice pre labour appreciation gift. Honestly she probably feels about as sexy as an elephant right now :eek: and while expensive trinkets are nice they wont do much for her ego!

A hamper of beauty treats, chocolate, etc could be nice too.

From baby...hmm...some sort of baby keepsake. One of those photo frames with a picture for each month of the first year, or some sort of album she can add to as time goes on. I like the hand print and foot print idea too.

If I could have anything right now it would be a big cup of ice...mmm! :rotfl:

posts.body:
Gte her a fantastic baby sling - it will benefit you both because she will be comfortable taking the baby out in public, and breastfeeding etc, and you wont be all cooped up inside getting angry at life!

slings also keep the baby close to mum's heartbeat which is critical in the early phase. the more heart beat, the happier the child in later life.

posts.body:
The eternity ring tradition is lovely if you have the funds & can avoid "that ring would buy a pram" issues.

Me, I had to take my wedding ring off, which stressed me a lot, and so my husband bought me its twin but bigger in a much lower carat gold. When I'd had our son, we inscribed his initials & date of birth into the ring which became our "maternity ring".

Oooh! A hamper of all the food I longed for and wasn't allowed to eat? Plus a really smelly blue cheese could have taken my nose off the meconium nappies...
